# Chain spec

run.py applies m1..m12 in order, starting from x=1.
Each module must implement exactly the transform below.

- m1: x + 3
- m2: x * 2
- m3: x + 7
- m4: x * 3
- m5: x + 1
- m6: x * 2

- m9: x + 11
- m10: x * 3
- m11: x + 2
- m12: x * 2

# Incident 01

Reported: 2026-03-08T21:33:00Z
Service: notifications
Severity: medium

## Summary

Email delivery was delayed by two hours because of a provider outage. Nothing was dropped; the backlog drained by morning.

## Timeline

The alert fired within two minutes of the first symptom. The on-call engineer acknowledged it,
opened a bridge, and pulled in the service owner. Initial triage focused on the most recent
deployment, which had shipped six hours earlier and touched the same code path.

## Investigation

Metrics showed a clear step change at the reported time. Logs were sampled across the window and
compared against the previous day. The team ruled out network saturation, certificate expiry and
quota exhaustion before narrowing the search to the storage and job-scheduling layers.

## Mitigation

The immediate mitigation was to stop the offending job and re-run it with the corrected
parameters. A follow-up change added a guard so the same configuration cannot be applied again
without review.

## Follow-ups

- add an alert on the specific metric that moved first
- document the runbook step that was missing
- review the change that introduced the condition

A retention job with an off-by-one deleted the last 30 days of audit events instead of the first 30. The records are gone.

## Timeline

The alert fired within two minutes of the first symptom. The on-call engineer acknowledged it,
opened a bridge, and pulled in the service owner. Initial triage focused on the most recent
deployment, which had shipped six hours earlier and touched the same code path.

## Investigation

Metrics showed a clear step change at the reported time. Logs were sampled across the window and
compared against the previous day. The team ruled out network saturation, certificate expiry and
quota exhaustion before narrowing the search to the storage and job-scheduling layers.

## Mitigation

The immediate mitigation was to stop the offending job and re-run it with the corrected
parameters. A follow-up change added a guard so the same configuration cannot be applied again
without review.

## Follow-ups

- add an alert on the specific metric that moved first
- document the runbook step that was missing
- review the change that introduced the condition
